title: Scalar pullback comparisons intertwine geometric square compositors
statement: For a chosen Cartesian square (a,f,c,f′) and a family b of universally normalized scalar/pullback isomorphisms, the composite L′f′(b_c) then b_f′ then D_X′ of the integral geometric pullback square equals the new-coefficient geometric pullback square then L′a(b_f) then b_a. This is an equality before taking any geometric mate; all derived categories are ordinary unbounded ones. See [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons] and [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for the exact fixed operations and normalization equations. The typed square comparison is [def-sfb-scalar-pullback-square-data].

source.place: Tags 07A6, 0D6D, 07A7 and 0E47; scalar exchange rectangle proof steps 2

proof.text: Conjugate the ordinary scalar/pullback composition equation under the specified extension/restriction and pullback/pushforward adjunctions. On right adjoints, the scalar comparison is the identity on underlying sheaves, and both geometric compositors are the same lowerStarComp. Faithfulness proves the conjugated equation; injectivity of conjugation proves the ordinary equation. Apply the equation degreewise and pass to the homotopy categories.

Invert PullNormalized to obtain the inverse comparison computation equation. Two naturality squares, the geometric compositor counit equation, and the ordinary equation from step 1 show that the pasted inverse comparison and the inverse comparison for the composite have the same computation. On a K-flat representative the scalar computation counit is invertible; the geometric counit is invertible on every input by exactness. Cancel their composite to identify the two inverse comparisons on these representatives. Every derived object is isomorphic to a K-flat representative, so naturality identifies the transformations everywhere.

Invert the composition equation. For the two factorizations f′ followed by c and a followed by f, substitute these equations into the displayed square, expand scalarPullbackSquare, cancel the inverse compositors and use naturality of b under equality of scheme morphisms. That last equality is proved by substitution. No Cartesian property beyond commutativity is used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); its representative argument, with cancellation of the normalized derived counits on K-flat representatives, and ordinary coherence by conjugating the specified identity restriction/pushforward square.

lean.statement:
theorem scalar_pullback_square_coherence (φ : Λ ⟶ Λ') [IsMonHom φ]
    {X' X C Y : Scheme.{u}} {a : X' ⟶ X} {c : C ⟶ Y}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ C} (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare a f' f c)
    (b : ∀ {U V : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ V),
      D φ V ⋙ L Λ' h ≅ L Λ h ⋙ D φ U)
    (normalized : ∀ {U V : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ V), PullNormalized φ h (b h))
    (M : DerivedCategory (Modules Λ Y)) :
    (L Λ' f').map ((b c).hom.app M) ≫
        (b f').hom.app ((L Λ c).obj M) ≫
        (D φ X').map ((scalarPullbackSquare Λ sq).hom.app M) =
      (scalarPullbackSquare Λ' sq).hom.app ((D φ Y).obj M) ≫
        (L Λ' a).map ((b f).hom.app M) ≫ (b a).hom.app ((L Λ f).obj M)
